content.problemStatement:
You receive an integer array `nums` and an integer `val`, remove all occurrences of `val` in `nums` [**in-place**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In-place_algorithm). The order of the elements may be changed. Then output *the number of elements in* `nums` *which are not equal to* `val`.

Consider the number of elements in `nums` which are not equal to `val` be `k`, to get accepted, you need to do the following things:

* Change the array `nums` such that the first `k` elements of `nums` contain the elements which are not equal to `val`. The remaining elements of `nums` are not important as well as the size of `nums`.
* The task is to output `k`.

**Custom Judge:**

The judge will test your solution with the following code:

```
int[] nums = [...]; // Input array
int val = ...; // Value to remove
int[] expectedNums = [...]; // The expected answer with correct length.
                            // It is sorted with no values equaling val.

int k = removeElement(nums, val); // Calls your implementation

assert k == expectedNums.length;
sort(nums, 0, k); // Sort the first k elements of nums
for (int i = 0; i < actualLength; i++) {
    assert nums[i] == expectedNums[i];
}
```

If all assertions pass, then your solution will be **accepted**.

notes: The judge compares the returned k with the expected number of retained elements.
For the retained prefix, element order is not required to match because the problem allows reordering.
This compacts all non-target values into the front of the array in place.
It preserves relative order, although preserving order is not required by the problem.
solution.approach: Use a write pointer k. Scan nums once; whenever nums[i] is not equal to val, write it to nums[k] and increment k. At the end, k is the number of retained elements and the first k positions contain all required values.

optimal.description: Maintain a write index k for the next position that should contain a value different from val. For each element, copy it to nums[k] only when it is not val, then increment k. The first k positions are exactly the required elements, and everything after k is irrelevant.

bruteForce.description: Scan the array and, whenever val is found, shift every later element one position to the left. Repeat until no val remains. Repeated shifting can make the worst-case running time quadratic.

followUps: Can you implement the solution without preserving the relative order of the retained elements?
What changes, if anything, if the array can contain duplicate values?
Can the solution remain O(1) extra space for a much larger array?
